title: The soldier who fought for 29 years after the war ended
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Onoda Hiroo' (sent to Lubang Island in December 1944, held out until 1974, relieved of duty by his former commander)

lines.text: In nineteen forty-four, a young Japanese officer was sent to a tiny island.
lines.caps: In *1944, | a young *officer | sent to a tiny *island.

lines.text: His orders were simple: never surrender.
A year later, the war ended.
But nobody he trusted came to tell him,
so he stayed hidden in the jungle, still fighting.
Leaflets said the war was over. He called them a trick.
In nineteen seventy-four, his old commander flew to the island
and gave him one last order: you can stop now.
He had fought for twenty-nine years, for a war that was already over.

hook: A soldier fought on for 29 years after his war ended
summary: Hiroo Onoda kept fighting in the Philippine jungle until 1974 because no one he trusted told him the war was over; his old commander finally relieved him.
